_purpose: Machine-readable actor-based flows for AI/coding tools — generate test cases, unit tests, automation. UC3 = 10-Second Skip Back/Forward for video / recorded-LS playback.
_status: Derived from PDT-3564-uc3-complete-jira-story.json (Layer 2 STEP 6, 2026-07-09 — NOT signed off). 11 ACs → 11 flows (1:1).
_warning: AC-11 (web ±10s skip during buffer) is PENDING FU-3 — flow-UC3-F11 carries an assumption flag (do not assert the skip result until FU-3 closes). Web rapid-tap debounce→accumulate (BR-08 / ledger GAP-07) is a dev delta — flagged as a plain assumption on flow-UC3-F06. Neither blocks its flow.
_precondition: UC3 depends on UC1a's controls overlay being visible. Flows that assume the overlay is already up set entry_from: 'flow-UC1a-F01'. F09 is the PRE-overlay baseline (entry_from: null). F08 is Live — its overlay is revealed by UC1b, not UC1a (see flow _note).
_coverage: happy_path: F01, F02, F06 · alternative: F03, F04, F05, F07, F10 · default_state: F08 (Live), F09 (baseline) · error_state: F11 (web buffer, FU-3). Every AC-01…AC-11 appears in exactly one flow.

actors.viewer: Community member watching a video / recorded livestream
actors.app: UIKit client UI — renders the controls overlay, the −10s / +10s skip buttons, and the skip icon feedback
actors.player: Playback engine — does the ±10s seek, clamps at boundaries (0:00 / final frame), buffers, and holds position + play/pause state
actors.sdk: Social+ SDK — reports stream type / room status (video, recorded LS, Live LS)
actors.network: Network layer delivering media data — stalls cause the player to buffer

flows.name: Skip back 10s during playback
flows.summary: Playing video, overlay up, position ≥10s from start — tap −10s → jumps back exactly 10s and keeps playing.

steps.action: taps the skip-back (−10s) button while the video is playing (position at least 10s from start, e.g. 1:00)
shows the −10 skip icon feedback
seeks playback back exactly 10 seconds from the current position
continues playback without interruption — skip is position-only and does not toggle play/pause

unit: player at 1:00, tap skip-back → assert seek issued with −10s → position 0:50
assert playback_state remains 'playing' after skip (BR-10)
assert skip icon text is '−10', never an accumulated total
scenario: play a video to 1:00, tap −10s → verify position 0:50 and video still playing
e2e: video playing at a known timecode → tap −10s → assert timecode decreased by exactly 10s and playback continues

flows.name: Skip forward 10s during playback
flows.summary: Playing video, overlay up, position ≥10s from end — tap +10s → jumps forward exactly 10s and keeps playing.

steps.action: taps the skip-forward (+10s) button while the video is playing (position at least 10s from end, e.g. 1:00)
shows the +10 skip icon feedback
seeks playback forward exactly 10 seconds from the current position
continues playback without interruption — skip is position-only and does not toggle play/pause

unit: player at 1:00, tap skip-forward → assert seek issued with +10s → position 1:10
assert playback_state remains 'playing' after skip (BR-10)
assert skip icon text is '+10', never an accumulated total
scenario: play a video to 1:00, tap +10s → verify position 1:10 and video still playing
e2e: video playing at a known timecode → tap +10s → assert timecode increased by exactly 10s and playback continues

flows.name: Boundary skip-back near start → clamp to 0:00, preserve prior state
flows.summary: Position <10s from start — tap skip-back → clamps to 0:00 (never negative) and PRESERVES prior state: playing continues from 0:00, paused stays paused. A boundary skip-back is NOT a forced pause.
flows._note: Corrects Jira AC-03 which still reads 'the video is in a paused state' — spec preserves prior state (AMB-11); PM to align Jira wording (FU-5). This is a resolved spec decision, not a pending clarification.

steps.action: taps skip-back while the current position is less than 10s from the start (e.g. 0:05), in either play state
shows the −10 skip icon feedback
clamps the seek to 0:00 — does not go to a negative position

state_change.note: clamped at start boundary; never negative

steps.action: preserves the prior playback state — if it was playing it continues from 0:00; if it was paused it stays paused (a boundary skip-back does NOT force a pause)

unit: video at 0:05 PLAYING, tap skip-back → assert position clamps to 0:00 AND playback_state still 'playing'
video at 0:05 PAUSED, tap skip-back → assert position 0:00 AND still 'paused' (NOT force-played, NOT force-paused)
assert position never resolves to a negative value
scenario: video at 0:05 playing → skip back → verify jumps to 0:00 and keeps playing (corrects Jira 'paused' wording, FU-5)
e2e: need videos of known length for boundary tests; seek to 0:05, tap −10s → assert position 0:00 AND prior play/pause state intact

flows.name: Boundary skip-forward near end → final frame, end state (paused)
flows.summary: Position within 10s of the end — tap skip-forward → clamps to the final frame and enters the end state (paused). Does not loop, does not error.

steps.action: taps skip-forward while the current position is within 10s of the end (e.g. a 2:00 video at 1:55)
shows the +10 skip icon feedback
clamps the seek to the final frame — does not seek past the end and does not loop back to 0:00

state_change.note: clamped at end boundary; never past final frame, never loops

steps.action: enters the end state — paused at the final frame (terminal condition; there is no content past the end to continue into)

unit: player at 1:55 of a 2:00 video, tap skip-forward → assert position clamps to final frame (2:00) AND end state (paused)
assert no loop back to 0:00 and no error thrown
scenario: video near end → skip forward → verify lands on final frame and is paused (end state)
e2e: need videos of known length for boundary tests; seek to within 10s of end → tap +10s → assert final frame + paused end state, no loop

flows.name: Skip while paused → position updates, stays paused
flows.summary: Video paused, overlay up — tap either skip button → position updates by ±10s but the video stays paused (skip does not auto-resume).

steps.action: taps either skip button while the video is paused (overlay visible)
shows the ±10 skip icon feedback for the tapped direction
updates the position by exactly ±10 seconds accordingly
remains paused — skip does not auto-resume playback

state_change.note: skip is position-only; does not auto-resume

unit: player paused at P, tap skip-forward → assert position P+10 AND playback_state still 'paused'
tap skip-back while paused → assert position updated AND playback NOT auto-resumed
scenario: pause the video → tap +10s → verify position advances 10s and video stays paused
e2e: pause playback → tap a skip button → assert timecode changes but play does not resume

flows.name: Rapid repeated taps accumulate; icon always shows ±10
flows.summary: Multiple quick taps each add ±10s (they accumulate — e.g. +10 ×3 at 1:00 → 1:30), while the skip icon always shows the per-tap value (+10 / −10), never the accumulated total.

assumptions.text: Web UIKit currently DEBOUNCES rapid taps to a single ±10s; to satisfy AC-07 / BR-08 web must change to ACCUMULATE (each tap adds ±10s). This is a dev delta (ledger GAP-07), not a spec gap — the flow is written to the TARGET accumulate behaviour. Mobile already accumulates.

steps.action: taps a skip button multiple times quickly (e.g. skip-forward ×3 while playing at 1:00)
shows the +10 skip icon on each tap — always the per-tap value, never the accumulated total (never '+30')

state_change.value: +10 shown per tap (not the accumulated total)

steps.action: accumulates every tap — each tap adds exactly 10 seconds to the target position
continues playback without interruption through the burst

unit: player at 1:00, dispatch 3 rapid skip-forward taps → assert final position 1:30 (accumulated, NOT 1:10)
assert skip icon text is '+10' on every tap, never '+30'
scenario: web: currently debounces — must accumulate; tap ×3 fast → assert net +30s (skip-forward) / −30s (skip-back)
mobile: tap ×3 fast → assert accumulated ±30s and icon only ever shows ±10
e2e: rapidly tap +10s three times → assert net +30s seek and the icon only ever shows +10 (regression guard for the web debounce fix)

flows.name: Rapid taps near boundary obey clamp mid-burst
flows.summary: During a rapid burst near the start/end, taps accumulate until one would cross the boundary — that tap follows the clamp rules (AC-03 / AC-04): it stops at 0:00 or the final frame, never negative, never loops, even mid-burst.

steps.action: taps a skip button multiple times quickly near the start or end (e.g. skip-back ×3 starting at 0:15)
shows the ±10 skip icon per tap
accumulates taps normally until a tap would cross the boundary
clamps the boundary-crossing tap mid-burst — lands at 0:00 (or the final frame) instead of a negative position or a loop

state_change.note: clamp applies mid-burst per AC-03/AC-04; never negative, never loops

unit: player at 0:15, 3 rapid skip-back taps → assert positions 0:05 then 0:00 (clamped) — never negative
burst near end → assert clamps at final frame mid-burst, no loop back to 0:00
scenario: need videos of known length for boundary tests; rapid −10s ×3 from 0:15 → verify ends at 0:00, never negative
rapid +10s ×N near the end → verify stops at the final frame, never loops
e2e: fast-tap −10s repeatedly near the start → assert timecode floors at 0:00 during the burst

flows.name: Live stream → no skip buttons (in-app)
flows.summary: On an active Live stream the ±10s skip buttons are NOT shown in the controls overlay — seeking is not applicable to Live (in-app). Recorded LS (after Live ends) uses the video player and DOES show them.
flows._note: Scope = in-app buttons only. The Live overlay is revealed by UC1b (not UC1a); web-live may have no reveal-controls overlay at all (impl delta). Android OS-native media-control scrub of a Live stream (lock screen / notification / car unit) is a SEPARATE bug (FU-4 / AMB-05), independent of AC-06 — see test_hints e2e.

steps.action: reports the stream status is Live (room status = live) — a Live LS, not video / recorded LS
renders the controls overlay for the Live stream
does NOT render the −10 / +10 skip buttons — seeking is not applicable on a Live stream (in-app)

unit: mock sdk stream type = Live → assert skip-back / skip-forward buttons NOT rendered in the overlay
mock sdk stream type = recorded LS → assert skip buttons ARE rendered (contrast case)
scenario: open a Live stream, reveal controls → verify no ±10s buttons; open that stream's recording → verify ±10s buttons present
e2e: Live stream overlay → assert absence of in-app skip buttons
OUT OF SCOPE for this flow: Android OS-native transport scrub on a Live stream (FU-4 bug), which is not an AC-06 gap

flows.name: Default baseline — no skip buttons before the overlay is revealed
flows.summary: A video / recorded LS is loaded but the UC1a controls overlay has not yet been revealed — no skip buttons are visible. They appear only as part of UC1a's overlay.
flows._note: Ties UC3's default state to UC1a's overlay lifecycle (build-order dependency UC1a → UC3). entry_from is null because this is the PRE-overlay baseline; revealing the overlay is UC1a (flow-UC1a-F01), after which F01–F07 / F10 / F11 apply.

steps.action: loads a video / recorded LS but has not yet tapped to reveal the controls overlay (per UC1a)
renders the video surface and plays
shows no skip buttons — the ±10s skip controls appear only as part of UC1a's controls overlay, which has not been revealed

unit: render the player fresh (overlay not revealed) → assert skip buttons absent from the tree
reveal the overlay (UC1a) → assert skip buttons now present (transition guard)
scenario: open a video without tapping → verify no ±10s buttons on screen until controls are revealed
e2e: load a video, do not tap → assert no skip buttons; tap to reveal (UC1a) → assert skip buttons appear

flows.name: Skip while buffering (mobile) → seek-and-rebuffer
flows.summary: On mobile, tapping a skip button while the player is buffering makes it seek to the target and rebuffer there — no stuck loading, no crash. Resolved by code (Prisa 68329).
flows._note: Mobile behaviour resolved by code — seek-and-rebuffer (Prisa 68329). The web equivalent is UNCONFIRMED — see flow-UC3-F11 / FU-3.

steps.action: delivers media data slowly at the current position (mobile), so the player cannot play smoothly
is in a buffering state at the current position
taps a skip button while the player is buffering
seeks to the target position and rebuffers there — surfaces a loading state at the new position, then resumes; no stuck loading, no crash

state_change.note: seek-and-rebuffer at target; explicit loading feedback, never a silent frozen frame

unit: put the mobile player in a buffering state, tap skip → assert a seek to the target is issued and buffering re-enters at the target (not stuck at the old position)
assert no crash and no infinite spinner
scenario: throttle the network to force buffering on mobile → tap +10s → verify the player rebuffers at the new position and eventually resumes
e2e: mobile: simulate buffering, tap skip → assert the target position loads (seek-and-rebuffer), no stuck loading

flows.name: Skip while buffering (web) → behaviour unconfirmed
flows.summary: On web, the exact behaviour of the ±10s skip tap while buffering is NOT yet confirmed (FU-3). Known: web separately shows a 'Reconnecting' UI and allows manual scrub/scroll — a different gesture from tapping the ±10s skip. Per BR-15 the viewer is never left on a silent frozen frame.

assumptions.text: Web ±10s skip behaviour mid-buffer is not yet confirmed (Owner: Web Engineering). The flow captures only what is known: web shows a 'Reconnecting' UI and allows manual scrub/scroll, which is a DIFFERENT gesture from the discrete ±10s skip tap. The skip-tap outcome itself is pending — do NOT assert a specific seek result until FU-3 closes.

steps.action: delivers media data slowly / stalls at the current position (web), so the player cannot play smoothly
is in a buffering state; the app surfaces the 'Reconnecting' UI (known behaviour) and manual scrub/scroll remains available
taps a ±10s skip button while buffering (distinct from the manual scrub/scroll gesture)
[PENDING FU-3] the exact outcome of the ±10s skip tap mid-buffer on web is not confirmed — the known 'Reconnecting' + manual scrub/scroll is a separate gesture, not the skip-tap result
[known / BR-15] never leaves the viewer on a frozen frame with no feedback — an explicit state (Reconnecting) is surfaced regardless of the skip outcome

state_change.value: explicit state surfaced (no silent frozen frame)

unit: [BLOCKED on FU-3] cannot assert the exact web skip-during-buffer seek result yet
assert web shows the 'Reconnecting' UI while buffering (known)
assert manual scrub/scroll remains available and is treated as a separate gesture from the ±10s skip
scenario: web: force buffering, tap ±10s → OBSERVE and record the behaviour to close FU-3 (do not assert until confirmed)
verify no silent frozen frame — the 'Reconnecting' state is visible (BR-15)
e2e: web: simulate a poor connection → assert the 'Reconnecting' UI appears; the ±10s skip outcome is DEFERRED pending FU-3
